s1.syndrome_frame: Subacute left leg pain and weakness with systemic inflammation
salient_findings: Increasing left leg pain and weakness over one week
Neurologic examination showing 4/5 strength in left hip and knee flexors and extensors
key_facts: 87-year-old man with multiple comorbidities
One week of increasing left leg pain and weakness
Impaired mobility
Single episode of urinary incontinence
Anorexia and 12% body-weight loss over six months
Blood pressure 88/45 mmHg responsive to IV fluids
Heart rate 96/min
Temperature 36.4 °C
Oxygen saturation 95% on room air
Elevated CRP and WCC
Pre-renal acute-on-chronic kidney injury
Neurologic examination showing 4/5 strength in left hip and knee flexors and extensors
Mild foraminal narrowing at L5–S1 on MRI
No central canal stenosis or abscess on MRI
Left hip pain worsened despite analgesia
Strength declined to 2/5 at the hip and 3/5 at the knee
CRP and ESR continued to rise
Small anterior joint effusion on left hip ultrasound
Normal tumour markers
MRI of the hip and isotope bone scan argued against malignancy
Bilateral iliacus and iliopsoas muscle oedema with enhancement on MRI

shortlist.label: Polymyalgia rheumatica
shortlist.why_kept: Subacute onset of leg pain and weakness with systemic inflammation, elevated CRP and ESR, and bilateral iliacus and iliopsoas muscle oedema

shortlist.label: Pyomyositis
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of muscle oedema and enhancement on MRI, along with systemic inflammation and elevated CRP

shortlist.label: Psoas abscess
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation of subacute leg pain and weakness, with evidence of muscle oedema and enhancement on MRI

shortlist.label: Inflammatory myopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated inflammatory markers, muscle weakness, and evidence of muscle oedema on MRI

shortlist.label: Septic arthritis
shortlist.why_kept: Systemic inflammation, elevated CRP and ESR, and presence of a small joint effusion on ultrasound

raw.rationale: Elevated inflammatory markers, muscle oedema with enhancement on MRI, and worsening symptoms despite analgesia are consistent with pyomyositis, a bacterial infection of the skeletal muscle

rejected.label: Polymyalgia rheumatica
rejected.why: Typically presents with proximal muscle pain and stiffness, but MRI findings of bilateral iliacus and iliopsoas muscle oedema are more suggestive of pyomyositis

rejected.label: Psoas abscess
rejected.why: MRI did not show evidence of an abscess

rejected.label: Inflammatory myopathy
rejected.why: Normal creatine kinase and lack of other characteristic features make this diagnosis less likely

rejected.label: Septic arthritis
rejected.why: Hip ultrasound and MRI did not show evidence of septic arthritis
